summary: Create a small board orchestration slice. The board owns aggregation and presentation policy; work-items and labels retain persistence, authorization, and independent change boundaries. The RSC page calls one authenticated board read entrypoint.

tree.purpose: Board view types, status-grouping rules, and Valibot schemas for board filters/output.
Orchestrates work-item and label operations; hides archived items, groups by status, attaches label details, and raises forbidden when any referenced label is not viewable.
Single declared application boundary: validates input/output, normalizes failures, and reports once.
Server-only authenticated read adapter; builds request context and invokes the board entrypoint.
Existing work-item persistence and actor-scoped read operation.
Existing label persistence and actor-scoped visibility resolution.
RSC route that calls the board read adapter and renders the returned board view.
Presentational board components receiving RSC data; no store or cross-slice imports.
Board policy tests using the real local data boundary or declared seam.
Work-item filtering, authorization, and row-mapping tests against the real store.
Label visibility and unauthorized-label behavior against the real store.
Authentication, authorization, and read-adapter outcome tests.
End-to-end authenticated board rendering and failure behavior.

flows: `load-board` entry validates filters, then calls `loadBoardOperation`; the operation requests actor-visible work items from the work-items public operation surface.
The board operation removes archived items, groups remaining items by status, collects referenced label IDs, and calls the labels public visibility operation with the same request context.
The labels capability enforces its own view policy and returns label details plus denied IDs; any denied referenced label becomes `forbidden`, rather than being silently omitted.
The operation builds the board view model → entry validates output → page renders `src/ui/board/*` as RSC props.

decisions.rationale: Aggregation, archive hiding, status grouping, label attachment, and cross-capability rejection are board behavior. Work-items calling labels would couple independent capabilities and assign board policy to the wrong owner.

The board operation may consume published work-item and label operations, while neither capability imports the other’s internals. Entries are not called from operations, preventing nested validation/reporting.

decisions.choice: Use existing local data modules; add no port
decisions.rationale: The stores are in-process/local application-owned persistence, so a port would add indirection without a current purposeful remote seam. If either capability is actually remote-owned, introduce a domain-language port and outbound adapter at that boundary.

decisions.choice: Reverify in the server-only read adapter and each data boundary
decisions.rationale: RSC rendering and route protection are not security boundaries. Request context carries actor identity; stores enforce actor visibility and never expose raw rows.

decisions.choice: Closed taxonomy through one board boundary
decisions.rationale: Validation, unauthorized, forbidden, contract, and unknown outcomes are normalized and reported once. Provider errors do not escape; the page maps kinds to user-safe rendering/navigation behavior.

decisions.choice: RSC-owned read with no client cache by default
decisions.rationale: This is a render-time read without polling, optimistic updates, or shared client lifecycle. Any cache tag must be actor/tenant scoped and invalidated by the owner of mutations.

decisions.choice: Test observable outcomes at each seam
decisions.rationale: Board policy is tested at the operation boundary, store policies against the real local engine, inbound auth/shape separately, and the complete contract through e2e.

risks: If existing work-item or label APIs expose only framework-bound entries rather than typed operations, extract their silent operations without making the board call nested declarations.
Parallel label loading is unsafe until work-item IDs are known; the flow is necessarily work-items first, labels second.
A label visibility denial must not reveal whether an inaccessible label exists beyond the declared `forbidden` outcome.
The proposal assumes local stores; remote or separately deployed capabilities would require ports and outbound adapters.
